sourcedFrom: Ruger P95 "Double Action Only" Model Instruction Manual — no edition code printed in this book — the cover page carries no text layer and no revision line appears anywhere in the document (no copyright year printed in this book — Ruger’s Southport, Connecticut address dates it to the earlier P-series printings, but the document itself states no year)
cleanIntro: Ruger publishes three different P95 books and this is the "DOUBLE ACTION ONLY" one. Every step below carries its words and the page they are printed on.

steps.title: Check you are on the right P95 book
steps.action: Before anything else, confirm your pistol is the "double action only" model — spurless hammer, no manual safety lever and no decocking lever. This manual is for that pistol and does not cover the manual-safety or decocker P95s, each of which Ruger gives its own book.
steps.prose: The other two P95 books each open by forbidding their use on this pistol. That matters here more than anywhere, because their first strip instruction tells you to work a control this gun does not have — and a control you cannot find is exactly when people start forcing things.
steps.aside: Spurless hammer. Does not have a “full cock” position and cannot be manually cocked.
steps.quote: This Instruction Manual is designed to assist you in learning how to use and care for your RUGER® P95 “Double Action Only” Model Pistols properly.
steps.cite: Ruger P95 "Double Action Only" Model Instruction Manual — no edition code printed in this book — the cover page carries no text layer and no revision line appears anywhere in the document — Firearms Safety - Your Responsibility, p.2

steps.title: Magazine out
steps.action: Keep the pistol pointed in a safe direction and press forward on the magazine latch, then withdraw the magazine from the butt.
steps.prose: This is the step that belongs to your variant and to no other — and what makes it yours is what is absent. There is no lever to set and no hammer to drop first; the magazine simply comes out.
steps.caution: Do not attempt to manually cock or “decock” the hammer!
steps.quote: Keep pistol pointed in a safe direction. Press forward on the magazine latch and withdraw magazine from butt of pistol.
steps.cite: Ruger P95 "Double Action Only" Model Instruction Manual — no edition code printed in this book — the cover page carries no text layer and no revision line appears anywhere in the document — To Disassemble, step 1, p.16
steps.warn: Always unload a firearm before cleaning, lubrication, disassembly or assembly.

steps.title: Lock the slide open and look
steps.action: Pull the slide to the rear and lock it open by pressing upward on the rear end of the slide stop, then confirm with your eyes that the chamber is empty.
steps.prose: Magazine out and chamber empty are two separate facts. Ruger repeats the chamber check here because the first one only proved the magazine was gone.
steps.quote: Pull slide to rear and lock in open position by pressing upward on rear end of slide stop. Again, be sure chamber is empty!
steps.cite: Ruger P95 "Double Action Only" Model Instruction Manual — no edition code printed in this book — the cover page carries no text layer and no revision line appears anywhere in the document — To Disassemble, step 2, p.16

steps.title: Push the ejector down and forward
steps.action: Keep upward pressure on the slide stop, reach a finger through the top of the slide, and push the ejector downward and forward until it locks in its lower position.
steps.prose: This is the step people miss and then force. Until the ejector is latched down the slide physically cannot run forward, and no amount of pulling will change that.
steps.caution: Open slide is under strong spring tension and could injure fingers if allowed to slam shut.
steps.quote: Insert finger through top of slide and push ejector downward and forward (see Figure 1, p. 17) until it locks in its lower position. This will permit forward movement of slide. Further disassembly is impossible unless this is done.
steps.cite: Ruger P95 "Double Action Only" Model Instruction Manual — no edition code printed in this book — the cover page carries no text layer and no revision line appears anywhere in the document — To Disassemble, step 3, p.16

steps.title: Line up the disassembly marks, pull the slide stop
steps.action: Grip the slide, press down on the slide stop and let the slide creep forward until the vertical disassembly line on the frame lines up with the one on the slide, then press in on the right-hand end of the slide stop and pull it out to the left.
steps.prose: The two vertical lines are the whole alignment. Note that Ruger’s own figure here is captioned as showing the decocker model — the marks and the motion are the same, the pistol in the drawing is not yours.
steps.quote: Now press down on slide stop and allow slide to move slowly forward until the vertical disassembly line on the frame is aligned with the vertical disassembly line on the slide (See Figure 2, p. 17). Press in on right-hand end of slide stop and pull slide stop out of frame to the left until it is withdrawn completely out of the frame.
steps.cite: Ruger P95 "Double Action Only" Model Instruction Manual — no edition code printed in this book — the cover page carries no text layer and no revision line appears anywhere in the document — To Disassemble, step 4, p.16

steps.title: Slide assembly off the front
steps.action: Push the slide forward and take the entire slide assembly off the front of the frame.
steps.prose: Straight off the front. With the slide stop out there is nothing left holding the two halves together.
steps.quote: Push slide forward and remove entire slide assembly to the front.
steps.cite: Ruger P95 "Double Action Only" Model Instruction Manual — no edition code printed in this book — the cover page carries no text layer and no revision line appears anywhere in the document — To Disassemble, step 5, p.16

steps.title: Camblock and recoil spring out
steps.action: Hold the slide upside down, lift the rear end of the camblock/recoil spring assembly to unseat it from the barrel lug, then withdraw it to the rear of the slide.
steps.prose: Lift the rear first — the assembly seats against the barrel lug, so trying to draw it straight back while it is still seated just binds it.
steps.quote: With slide held upside down, lift rear end of camblock/recoil spring assembly to disengage it from its seat against the barrel lug. Withdraw the camblock/recoil spring assembly to the rear of the slide.
steps.cite: Ruger P95 "Double Action Only" Model Instruction Manual — no edition code printed in this book — the cover page carries no text layer and no revision line appears anywhere in the document — To Disassemble, step 6, p.16

steps.title: Barrel out
steps.action: Pull the barrel slightly upward out of the slide and withdraw it to the rear.
steps.prose: Up a little, then back. The tilting-barrel lockup means it has to clear its recess before it will travel.
steps.quote: Pull barrel upward out of slide slightly and withdraw to the rear.
steps.cite: Ruger P95 "Double Action Only" Model Instruction Manual — no edition code printed in this book — the cover page carries no text layer and no revision line appears anywhere in the document — To Disassemble, step 7, p.16

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Frame, slide, barrel, camblock/recoil spring assembly and magazine — that is the whole strip Ruger documents for the "double action only" P95.
steps.prose: This is as far as the book goes, and it is far enough to clean the pistol properly.
steps.quote: This completes normal fieldstripping for routine cleaning and lubrication purposes. Further disassembly of slide or frame components is not recommended and should only be undertaken by the factory.
steps.cite: Ruger P95 "Double Action Only" Model Instruction Manual — no edition code printed in this book — the cover page carries no text layer and no revision line appears anywhere in the document — To Disassemble, step 8, p.16

deepAbsentReason: Ruger ends this book’s disassembly at step 8: "Further disassembly of slide or frame components is not recommended and should only be undertaken by the factory." It documents nothing past the field strip, so this listing has NO deep clean. That is the manual’s answer, not a gap in ours.

cleaning.name: BORE & CHAMBER
tasks: Run a solvent-wetted patch through the bore several times with a cleaning rod
Attach a solvent-wetted bristle brush and run it back and forth the full length of the bore as many times as needed to clear grease and dirt from bore and chamber
Clean the bore with dry patches and examine it — Ruger warns bore fouling costs accuracy and grease in the chamber interferes with feeding from the magazine

cleaning.name: ALL COMPONENTS OF THE MECHANISM
tasks: Remove powder residue from every component with powder solvent on a clean patch or bristle brush
Run a dry patch through the bore, then follow it with a very lightly oiled one
Wipe all surfaces clean with cloth, then wipe them with a patch or cloth that is very lightly oiled

cleaning.name: MAGAZINE
tasks: Check the follower moves freely and has enough tension to lift each cartridge to the feeding position
Check the magazine lips are clean and free of cracks, dents or nicks
After soaking a dirty magazine, shake it vigorously with the loading opening away from you — Ruger warns solvent left inside can kill primers or weaken powder

cleaning.name: BEFORE YOU SHOOT IT AGAIN
tasks: Remove all oil and grease from the bore before firing
Keep the oil light — Ruger warns excess oil attracts dust and can congeal in cold weather

reassembly: Be certain the chamber and magazine are empty.
With the slide held upside down, replace the barrel and push it rearward into its locked position.
Replace the camblock and recoil spring assembly — the rear end of the camblock seats against the barrel lug.
Be certain the ejector is locked in its lower (forward) position and the hammer is in its fired (uncocked) position.
Replace the slide onto the frame and partially insert the slide stop.
Pull the slide back until the disassembly line on the frame lines up with the disassembly line on the slide stop, then push the slide stop all the way through the frame to the right.
Allow the slide to move fully forward.
Replace the empty magazine through the butt — that is what returns the ejector to its working position. Ruger warns the pistol will not function normally unless the ejector is up (rearward).
